openings.claim: A guided short-stroke sliding mass proposes repeated axial impulses to seat the rail; a stop referencing an unvarnished surface is the proposed face-protection dependency.
openings.discriminator: Predicts less lateral drift than D2 under identical alignment errors; superiority is unknown. A varnish strike or failure to seat defeats it.
openings.probe: On sacrificial geometries, compare D1/D2 drift and flush seating with deliberate alignment offsets; inspect every contact mark and verify travel stays within 35 mm.
openings.uncertainty: Stop positioning and sufficient impulse within permitted travel are untested.

openings.claim: A bent flexure with an indispensable sleeved head proposes elastic storage to concentrate a short hand-input stroke at rail contact.
openings.discriminator: Predicts adequate seating where D1 stalls, with worse aim; failure to seat or visible-face contact defeats that prediction.
openings.probe: First establish sleeve fabricability; if feasible, compare surrogate seating and aim with D1 under matched offsets, inspect contacts, verify 35 mm travel, and assess fatigue.
openings.uncertainty: Sleeve availability and flexure fatigue are unknown; infeasible sleeve stops this route. No constraint relaxation is requested.

lineage.reason: Retains guided impulses, unvarnished-stop dependency, comparative drift prediction, and failure gates.
Retains elastic concentration, indispensable sleeve, seating/aim tradeoff, and feasibility/failure gates.
Longer travel predicts greater speed/impulse but exceeds 35 mm. Seating benefit and bruising remain unknown; no in-case trial, and surrogate study cannot remove the violation.

decision: All proposals are hypothetical; no measured or comparative evidence exists. Prioritize sleeve feasibility and stop geometry before surrogate comparison. Success requires flush seating without visible-edge bruising, zero visible-varnished-face contact, travel entirely inside the 35 mm recess, and no cabinet alteration. Only an assumed geometry sketch exists; no tool or workpiece is supplied.
